purpose: 13 questions sourced verbatim from plan §7.17. Author runs through these once when ready, paraphrases the answers into the matching MDX section, then sets `interviewComplete: true` in about.mdx frontmatter.

questions: In one sentence, who are you and what do you do? (No 'engineer at a top company' — what makes YOU you?)
What's the one thing you'd want a recruiter to know about you in the first 5 seconds of landing on this page?
If you had to summarize your engineering identity in 3 words, what would they be?
Why does this site exist? (What problem does it solve for *you*, not for the recruiter?)
Who is this site really for? (Be honest — is it a recruiter, future you, your community, all three?)
What's the one thing you hope visitors take away from spending time here?
Walk me through how you got into engineering. What was the spark? (Specific moment if you can remember one.)
What was the hardest moment in your engineering education or early career? What did you learn from it?
What's a project or course that fundamentally changed how you think? Why?
Tell me about a moment when something clicked. The 'aha' you remember most vividly.
What's a failure or mistake you're glad happened, in retrospect?
Where do you want to be in 5-10 years, and why? (Avoid generic; be specific about the *kind* of work.)
What's the one piece of advice you'd give a younger version of yourself entering this field?
